newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel buries former president Herzog.
newsitem.headline: Israel buries former president Herzog.

text.p: Israel buried its former President Chaim Herzog on Friday, hailing him as a man of many talents who had fought for Israel on both the battlefield and the world stage.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who like Herzog was an ambassador to the United Nations, spoke at the burial ceremony at Jerusalem's Mount Herzl. Herzog died on Thursday at age 78.

At the United Nations in 1975, he took the podium of the General Assembly and ripped up a draft resolution that equated Zionism -- the belief in a Jewish state -- with racism. Years later he welcomed the U.N. decision to rescind the resolution.

"Herzog pushed back the attacks on Israel at the United Nations out of a deep personal belief and that's what explains the great talent that emerged there and the special way that he paved for all of those who came after him," Netanyahu said.

The Irish-born Herzog, who immigrated to Israel before its 1948 founding, crammed into his life at least half a dozen careers. More than 20 years in the military, he also practiced law, wrote books, and served as the sixth president for a decade until 1993 when he was succeeded by President Ezer Weizman.

"More than anything he understood our uniqueness as one people, as a people made up of all its roots, all its branches," said Netanyahu, who is awaiting a decision by state prosecutors on whether he will be charged in a corruption scandal.

"There was no man more suitable to stand at the head of the celebrations of the country's jubilee year and so I appointed him to this job. Fate dictated that he won't see this jubilee but the country will celebrate in his spirit and we'll dedicate the best of our efforts to reach his height," Netanyahu said.

Throughout the six days of the 1967 Middle East war, as a reserve major-general, Herzog offered commentary on local radio in the days before television in Israel, acting as the widely perceived "valium" to a nervous nation.

He took part in the 1944 Normandy landings with the British, was with the first troops to cross the Rhine and became Field Marshal Bernard Montgomery's personal representative to a high-level conference on displaced Europeans after the war.
